2nd Nov to 6th Nov
•	Two tractors with implements have been delivered to local farmers. This support is expected to benefit approximately 1,000 farmers and contribute to the cultivation of around 10,000 feddans of land. The machinery 
•	The handover of the machinery was attended by representatives from the local authorities (Executive Director, Head of Police , community leaders, the Community Management Committee (CMC), and beneficiary representatives.
•	During the handover ceremony, some community leaders expressed concerns about the machinery being allocated to a limited number of individuals, emphasizing that the support should benefit all farmers in Tokar. In response, the Executive Director clarified that the selected beneficiaries had been identified through consultations with representatives from all community groups. Nevertheless, it was agreed to hold further discussions with the community leaders to find a more inclusive solution
•	A field survey was conducted to verify and confirm the information of eligible beneficiaries for the goat distribution program, covering a total of 63 families within the targeted communities.
•	A youth needs assessment survey was carried out to identify interests and preferred types of vocational training, engaging 80 young men and 125 young women.
•	A leadership training workshop was organized for community committee members, with a focus on 15 women participants.
The training aimed to enhance leadership and community engagement capacities and covered the following key topics:
o	The concept and essential qualities of effective leadership
o	Communication and interpersonal skills
o	Teamwork and collaboration
o	Practical application of communication techniques
o	Leadership and decision-making processes
o	Identifying and responding to community needs
o	Group discussions and experience sharing

Red Sea Org – JSB: 
1. Under the activity 3.1 Capacity Building training conducted for 30 Smallholder Farmers (13 females and 17 males).
The facilitators of this training was the agricultural officers from Sinkat Locality who were trained by RSO two weeks ago.  They facilitate training on vegetable cultivation. 
The training combined both theoretical sessions and practical field visits, including on-site demonstrations in agricultural fields, which enhanced participants’ understanding of modern and sustainable vegetable farming practices.
Notably, the trainees took a proactive initiative by establishing an agricultural association under the umbrella of RSO, aiming to ensure sustainability, , and continuity of agricultural activities after the end of the project. This initiative demonstrates strong community ownership and commitment to long-term impact.

2. Procurement of Agricultural Seedlings
As part of the preparation for the proposed farming program, the following seedlings were procured this week:
150 mango seedlings
100 guava seedlings
100 lemon seedlings
25 date palm seedlings.

Toker Locality – Betay Development Organization
Activity 1.1 – Agricultural Support to Host Communities
•	A package of agricultural tools (hoes, shovels, and axes) was distributed to 100 male farmers from host communities to strengthen agricultural productivity and field preparation.
Activity 1.4 – Women’s Economic Empowerment
1. Office Based Income Generation Group (8 Women)
•	A group of 8 women received: 
o	Photocopier
o	Printer
o	Computer
•	This support will enable the group to launch a documentation and printing service, creating a sustainable income generation opportunity.
2. Tent Rental Business Group (10 Women)
•	A second group of 10 women received five water barrels.
•	This group had previously received tents and has already initiated a tent rental business.
•	The additional water barrels enhance their operational capacity and service delivery.
1. Distribution of Food Processing Inputs and Tools – Hoshiri Center Area
•	Women’s groups successfully received food production inputs and processing equipment, enabling them to start production activities immediately.
•	A joint production and work plan was developed, emphasizing collective effort. A selected subgroup of women was assigned responsibility for marketing the products.
•	The groups agreed to hold weekly meetings to discuss income management and monitor sales performance.
•	Initial manufactured products include: 
o	Balah Al Sham
o	Biscuits
•	A structured sales schedule was developed to organize production and distribution.
•	Products are marketed through multiple channels, such as: 
o	Home based sales
o	Sales at events, schools, and local markets
•	Feedback from the groups indicates that sales are faster and more profitable at gatherings compared to home-based sales.
2. Distribution of Food Processing Inputs and Tools – Village Area
•	Food processing inputs and equipment have been prepared for distribution to women’s groups in the village, with plans to launch production activities soon.
3. Distribution of Small Ruminants to Vulnerable Households
Milk Production and Household Impact
•	Follow-up with beneficiary households shows that sheep and goats provide approximately 3–3.5 pounds of milk per day, offering a valuable source of nutrition.
•	Productivity levels are reported as high and consistent.
Household Benefits
•	Household A: 
o	The mother, father, and four children benefit from daily milk that is sufficient for preparing dinner, morning tea, and producing yogurt.
•	Household B: 
o	Milk production exceeds the household’s own needs and also supports the sister’s family, demonstrating strong nutritional and social value
